paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Paul isn't handing out a rule just to fence you in. He's telling believers who they are: "we are the temple of the living God." Then he says, "Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers." A yoke ties two together to pull the same way, so being yoked to an unbeliever means being hitched to someone pulling the other way, and you get a whole lot of circles (2 Corinthians 6:14, 16).

So why does this matter to you? Because God doesn't just say "come out." He says, "I will dwell with them and walk among them," and then, "I will receive you." Then He tops it off with "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters." Nobody gets sent away empty-handed here. The separating is the part you do, and the Father does the welcoming, and that is a GOOD trade (2 Corinthians 6:16-18).

Then Paul calls you "beloved," and he says "since we have these promises," so the cleaning comes AFTER the love, not before it. You aren't scrubbing to earn a spot in the house. You're tidying up because you already live there. So go on, baker, keep "perfecting holiness in the fear of God," one drawer at a time (2 Corinthians 7:1).
